stories.headline: Sydney police step up armed patrols after Bondi terror attack
stories.title: Sydney police step up armed patrols after Bondi terror attack
stories.summary: Sydney, Oct 8 : Heavily armed police will be deployed across Australia's Sydney ahead of a rapid response unit established in the wake of the Bondi Beach terror attack becoming fully operational. The government of the Australian state of New South Wales (NSW) on Thursday said that officers from the state police force's new Armed Response Command (ARC) will begin patrolling Sydney over the coming weeks as the unit's training moves into realistic environments. The ARC was established as a permanent unit by the state government following the fatal mass shooting of 15 people at a Jewish holiday celebration at Bondi Beach in December last year, Xinhua News Agency reported. NSW Premier Chris Minns, Police and Counter-terrorism Minister Yasmin Catley and Police Commissioner Mal Lanyon said in a statement on Thursday that ARC officers will patrol high-risk areas, including places of worship and major events, and rapidly respond to emerging threats. The 250-officer unit will have access to combat assault rifles and 24 purpose-built vehicles and will be supported by a specialised operations centre. "Keeping the people of New South Wales safe is our number one priority. That means making sure our police have the people, training and equipment they need to respond to serious threats," Minns said. Lanyon said that the ARC would act as a deterrent for anyone who wishes to commit harm, incite hatred or cause fear. In February, accused Bondi Beach terror attack perpetrator Naveed Akram made his first appearance in a Sydney court after being charged with 59 offences over the fatal mass shooting. Akram appeared on Monday morning via video link from a supermax prison where he has been held since being discharged from the hospital in the wake of the attack on December 14, 2025. The 24-year-old was charged with 59 offences, including 15 counts of murder and one count of committing a terrorist act, in relation to the attack. Authorities allege that Akram and his father, Sajid, who was shot dead by police at the scene of the attack, opened fire on a Jewish celebration at the iconic eastern Sydney beach using rifles and shotguns, killing 15 people and injuring dozens more. Court documents made public in December 2025 revealed that police found evidence that the two attackers had conducted firearms training at a rural property before the attack. Local media reported that Akram was mostly silent during the administrative hearing and only spoke when directly addressed by the presiding Magistrate. --IANS

stories.headline: Cotton University and Gauhati University Wrapped up their Respective Student Union Election Results, with the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) Sweeping Key Posts
stories.title: Cotton University and Gauhati University Wrapped up their Respective Student Union Election Results, with the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) Sweeping Key Posts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'election results' in title weight 64
article_sentences: Campus politics in Assam reached a fever pitch as the Cotton University Students' Union (CUSU) and Gauhati University Postgraduate Students' Union declared their final election results.
In a stellar performance at Cotton University, the All Assam Students' Union (AASU) asserted its dominance by securing seven key seats.
Driven heavily by support from the landmark RKB and NBD hostels, AASU-backed candidate Hari Prasad Chetia clinched the position of President, while Ujjal Deka emerged victorious as General Secretary.
The election recorded a strong voter turnout of approximately 55%, with 3,309 votes polled.
"This victory reflects the students' unwavering trust in our vision for structural updates and academic welfare," stated a triumphant AASU campus representative.
Meanwhile, competing student wings including the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP) and Satra Mukti Sangram Samiti (SMSS) also managed to claim various portfolios in a sharply divided mandate.
Concurrently, Gauhati University finalized its count after initial delays.
The results saw a close fight where AASU won seven posts, tightly trailed by ABVP with six seats, confirming a vibrant, multi-faction leadership landscape across Guwahati's top premium institutions.

stories.headline: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma to visit Jamugurihat LAC Today
stories.title: Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma to visit Jamugurihat LAC Today
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: JAMUGURIHAT: Assam Chief Minister Dr Himanta Biswa Sarma is scheduled to visit Jamugurihat of the Naduar Assembly constituency on Thursday as part of a daylong programme, during which he will inaugurate several development schemes and industrial projects.

The Chief Minister’s first programme will be at the Kanyaka Marketing Society’s dairy production centre, where he will inaugurate a newly added milk-processing project with a capacity of 20,000 litres.

He will thereafter proceed to the Chowkighat area, where he will inaugurate a tile manufacturing factory constructed at Gataimari Chapori in the western part of Jamugurihat and located in the eastern part of Chowkighat bridge, the second bridge over the Jiya Bharali river.
The Chief Minister will also perform the Bhoomi Pujan for a proposed Limca factory in the same area.

A public meeting will also be held at Chowkighat, where land allotment documents will be distributed among 52 SHGs comprising 520 local unemployed youths who have been engaged in agricultural activities in the area.
CM Dr Sarma will subsequently proceed to Tyagbir Hem Baruah College, where he is scheduled to interact with students.

stories.headline: India exposes Pak doublespeak at UN, says world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11 and Pahalgam attacks
stories.title: India exposes Pak doublespeak at UN, says world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11 and Pahalgam attacks
stories.summary: United Nations, Oct 08: Exposing Pakistan’s doublespeak on terrorism at the UN, India has called out Islamabad’s efforts to gloss over its state support for terror by announcing rewards for JeM chief Masood Azahar, underlining that the world has not forgotten 9/11, 26/11 and Pahalgam attacks. India on Wednesday exercised its Right of Reply in response to the Pakistan representative’s statement in the Sixth Committee of the UN General Assembly on the Agenda Item: Measures to Eliminate International Terrorism. “Pakistan speaks of combating terrorism while seeking to obscure the very question that this committee must confront: What happens when terrorists are financed, facilitated, trained, sheltered, or supported from the territory of a state?” First Secretary in the Permanent Mission of India to the UN Raghoo Puri said. He said India has been consistent on this question, underscoring that terrorism cannot be defeated by declarations and instead requires action against its perpetrators, organisers, financiers, and sponsors. “For years, Pakistan has presented itself as a frontline state in combating terrorism and as a victim while masking the fact that the Frankensteins the Pakistani state has created and lost control over have moved from wreaking havoc in neighbouring countries to doing the same in Pakistan,” Puri said. Calling out Pakistan’s doublespeak on terrorism, Puri said the country “glosses over its state support for terrorism by announcing enhanced rewards for apprehending UN-listed head of Jaish-e-Mohammed terrorist and mastermind of several attacks against my country, Masood Azhar.” He said the world is aware of Pakistan's financial support to terrorism. “Yet, we also remember that just a few months ago, Pakistani representatives used this forum to call the Jaish-e-Mohammed a defunct organisation. The world has seen the script play earlier, and we are clear-eyed that this time also it is going to be no different,” he said. Puri said that when the media can reach Azhar and get confirmation from him about the success of Operation Sindoor, "surely the Pakistani state knows his whereabouts”. In May last year, India had launched Operation Sindoor targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in retaliation for the dastardly April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam in Jammu and Kashmir perpetrated by The Resistance Front, a proxy of Pakistan-based terror group Lashkar-e-Taiba, in which 26 civilians, mostly tourists were killed. Earlier this month, India had dismissed as “gimmicks” Pakistan’s fresh announcement of a bounty of seven million rupees on Azhar, demanding that Islamabad take “concrete action” to combat terrorism. India has for years accused Pakistan of sheltering Azhar, while Pakistan has maintained that he fled to Afghanistan – a claim rejected by Afghanistan’s Taliban government. For the last few years, Islamabad has claimed that the JeM founder has been operating from Afghanistan. However, the Taliban regime dismissed Pakistan’s repeated claims, with a senior Afghan Foreign Ministry official saying he is not in the country. Islamabad’s fresh announcement on the reward for information on Azhar came as it faces pressure from the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) to crack down on terror groups and their leadership. The Paris-based global watchdog is set to review Pakistan’s anti-terrorism efforts at its upcoming plenary. Pakistan was placed under the FATF grey list between 2018 and 2022 for its systemic deficiencies in anti-money laundering and its failure to counter-terror financing. Puri also recalled a recent statement by Punjab Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, daughter of former Pakistan prime minister Nawaz Sharif, who had said,“The unfortunate thing is that the threat [Punjab] faces comes less from my neighbouring countries and more from my neighbouring provinces.” Exposing this “dark secret”, Puri said, “You cannot run with the hares and hunt with the hounds. Reality never works like that.” “When terrorist groups are allowed to operate under state political power, international commitments become meaningless and when perpetrators are provided safe havens, the victims of terrorism are denied justice,” he said. “The world has not forgotten 9/11 and where its perpetrators, including Osama bin Laden, were caught. The world has not forgotten 26/11. The world has not forgotten Pahalgam,” Puri said, adding that the list, “unfortunately”, is painfully long. “The victims in Pahalgam were not asked about their political orientation, they were asked about their religion. It is therefore deeply ironic that Pakistan speaks of combating religious hatred while allowing the conditions that enable it to persist and thrive, especially by fomenting cross-border terrorism,” he said. “Pakistan continues with its narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation. If bombed-out airfields and cratered runways look like victory to Pakistan, they are of course welcome to enjoy it," Puri said. "Any regime against terrorism to be effective must do two things: assign responsibility and ensure accountability. India will defend its people, and continued terrorism against India will have consequences,” he added. In another Right of Reply, Puri said India rejected Pakistan’s “circular economy” of words and narratives. “If this much effort had actually been made in countering terrorism rather than narrative building, misinformation, and disinformation, the world would have been a better place. But nothing more can be expected from a Form 47 government,” he said, referring to a term used to describe allegations of rigging and manipulation in Pakistan’s 2024 general elections.

stories.headline: Israel says British Consulate in east Jerusalem ceases to function after dispute
stories.title: Israel says British Consulate in east Jerusalem ceases to function after dispute
stories.summary: Jerusalem, Oct 08: Israel said on Thursday that the British Consulate in east Jerusalem has “ceased to function” in that capacity and that 20 staffers would leave the country, the latest in what has been the biggest diplomatic friction between the close allies in decades. Britain said the building would continue to deliver “vital services” and work with Palestinians, and that it would not retaliate by expelling Israeli diplomats as it seeks to rebuild its staff. The sign outside the consulate was taken down. The dispute began last month when the United Kingdom banned trade with Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. The United Nations and much of the international community consider all settlements as illegal. “Israel will no longer turn its cheek to diplomatic attacks against it," Israeli Foreign Minister Gideon Saar said in a statement, adding that the building would continue to operate with a “task force” of seven diplomats and a “very limited” scope of activity. Twenty British diplomats will leave Israel, including the consul general. British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said in a statement that the building "will be known as the UK Mission, Jerusalem” after discussions with Israel's government, and a small team of diplomats would continue to operate there. “This will ensure that we maintain our longstanding British presence and the UK's role in support of a two-state solution,” Miliband added. Britain had threatened to expel Israeli diplomats if the consulate was closed, but said it would not do so for now because it's in talks with Israel about increasing the UK presence at the mission. “We will work in the coming months to build back up our presence,” Miliband said. Meanwhile, “our diplomats are going to be able to carry out their important work in relation to, for example, relations with the Palestinians, but also supporting British nationals visiting the area,” Middle East Minister Stephen Doughty told Times Radio. Miliband made clear that Britain does “not accept that the government of Israel has the legal right to close the British Consulate General in Jerusalem, which has been there for nearly 200 years.” The foreign secretary added that the UK government reiterates its view that east Jerusalem "is occupied territory." Israel captured the West Bank, along with Gaza and East Jerusalem, in the 1967 Middle East war, territories the Palestinians want for a future state. Since then, the Israeli government has built scores of settlements that are home to well over 500,000 Jewish settlers. Many settlements resemble fully developed suburbs. The current government under Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, the most nationalist and religious in Israel's history, views the West Bank as the biblical and historical homeland of the Jewish people and sees the settlements as key to maintaining security.

stories.headline: India’s 3-Point Ukraine Truce Plan: Kyiv Praises India’s ‘Most Comprehensive’ Proposal
stories.title: India’s 3-Point Ukraine Truce Plan: Kyiv Praises India’s ‘Most Comprehensive’ Proposal
stories.summary: India has moved beyond calling for dialogue in the Russia-Ukraine war and put forward a broader ceasefire proposal covering three key areas: attacks on energy infrastructure, the movement of grain and energy through Black Sea ports, and the safety of commercial shipping. Ukraine says it has received four ceasefire proposals — from India, the US, Türkiye and Egypt — and has described India’s as the “most comprehensive.” The development comes as Russian President Vladimir Putin praises Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s peace efforts and says Modi raises the Ukraine conflict at his meetings with him. India’s approach focuses on areas where both Moscow and Kyiv have immediate interests, rather than attempting to resolve every territorial and security dispute at once. For New Delhi, the stakes are also practical. Disruptions in the Black Sea affect food, energy, fertiliser and trade flows, with recent damage to Black Sea infrastructure already disrupting India-bound Russian sunflower oil shipments.

stories.headline: When Nana Patekar sought to join Army at Kargil front, spent 60 days with troops
stories.title: When Nana Patekar sought to join Army at Kargil front, spent 60 days with troops
stories.summary: Mumbai, Oct 8 : At the height of the Kargil War in 1999, Nana Patekar put his acting career on hold and sought permission to join the Indian Army at the war front, a chapter of his life that the veteran actor recalled years later during his appearance on "Kaun Banega Crorepati". Patekar, who died on Thursday at the age of 76 due to cardiac arrest in Goa, had rigourously trained with armed forces for his 1991 movie Prahaar: The Final Attack , in which he essayed the role of Major VS Chavan. He trained with the Maratha Light Infantry for three years for the film, which he had also written and directed. When the Kargil conflict broke out, Patekar approached senior army officers with a request to join the troops but was told that such permission could only be granted by the Defence Minister. "I knew our Defence Minister George Fernandes ji, so I called him. Even he said it was impossible," Patekar told megastar Amitabh Bachchan when he appeared on KBC in August 2024 when he was promoting the movie Vanvaas . "I told him, 'Commission toh six months mein hota hai, maine toh teen saal guzaare hain .' He asked where, and I told him about my experience with the Maratha Light Infantry. stories.headline: Tariff Is to Be Decided by Operators, Says TRAI Chairman: Report
stories.title: Tariff Is to Be Decided by Operators, Says TRAI Chairman: Report
stories.summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) cannot act on “guesswork” over reports of a possible 10-15 percent telecom tariff ... Read More
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: - TRAI Chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti said telecom tariffs are to be decided by operators under the current forbearance regime.
- TRAI will intervene on tariff hikes only when there is a necessity for regulatory action, Lahoti said.
- TRAI says consumers should have the choice to subscribe to plans based on their requirements.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) cannot act on “guesswork” over reports of a possible 10-15 percent telecom tariff hike, TRAI Chairman Anil Kumar Lahoti reportedly said, while reiterating that operators must comply with the regulator’s mandate to offer voice- and SMS-only plans despite industry pushback.
Speaking to CNBC-TV18, Lahoti said telecom tariffs are currently under a forbearance regime, under which operators are free to determine their prices.
He said market forces are driving tariffs in India’s competitive telecom sector, while TRAI continues to monitor developments.
“As far as tariff is concerned, as per the present regulatory provisions, the tariff is under forbearance, which means the tariff is to be decided by operators,” Lahoti reportedly said.
Asked whether TRAI would intervene if operators raised tariffs by 10-15 percent, Lahoti reportedly said, “I don’t think we can act on this based on guesswork.
As soon as there is a necessity of intervention, we’ll do that.”
He also pointed to the level of competition in the sector, saying tariffs in India are “probably the lowest in the world”.
On TRAI’s mandate for voice- and SMS-only plans, Lahoti reportedly said the regulator has not received a response from operators but stressed that the requirement is already part of the regulations.

“We haven’t received a response, but this is a regulation which has already been issued, and the operators are required to comply with this,” he was quoted as saying in a report dated October 6, 2026.

stories.headline: RBI may deliver 50 bps ‘jumbo’ hike in December, repo rate seen at 6%: SBI Research
stories.title: RBI may deliver 50 bps ‘jumbo’ hike in December, repo rate seen at 6%: SBI Research
stories.summary: The report expects inflation to peak at around 6.8% in November 2026
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'repo rate' in title weight 42
article_sentences: The Reserve Bank of India could raise the repo rate by another 50 basis points to 6 per cent by December, while taking additional measures to support the rupee, SBI Research said in its latest report, as it flagged rising inflation pressures and capital outflows.

The report said the October policy marked a shift from “watchfulness to explicit tightening”, with the RBI raising the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50 per cent and moving its stance from neutral to calibrated tightening.
The policy options in the near term are now effectively limited to a rate hike or a pause, depending on inflation and growth conditions.
"Peak policy rate poised for 6%...
our estimates now point towards a jumbo rate hike of 50 bps," SBI Research said, adding that “a 6% repo rate by December could be the best possible option.”
The report expects inflation to peak at around 6.8 per cent in November 2026.
Based on historical policy cycles, it estimates that the peak repo rate could be around 6 per cent, implying another 50 basis points of tightening from the current level.
However, it said the pace and quantum of hikes would depend on the inflation trajectory and global conditions.
SBI Research also proposed a series of measures to support the rupee, which it said had fallen to a five-month low.
The report noted that debt outflows totalled $2.1 billion in September as the dollar strengthened rapidly.

To encourage longer-term equity inflows, it suggested a graded long-term capital gains structure for investments held beyond a reasonable period, such as three years, while maintaining some parity with domestic investors.
It also proposed widening the effective interest rate corridor by raising the Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) rate, even for a limited period, without changing the policy rate.

A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana prima facie observed that a 2025 Jharkhand rule, which allowed an officer with residual service of less than 6 months before superannuation to be considered for DGP Appointment, was contrary to the law laid down by the Court in Prakash Singh case.

Considering that annulment of the rule could affect the appointment of Jharkhand DGP, Smt Tadasha Mishra, it issued notice to Mishra, so she can have an opportunity of being heard.

In the alternative, it may file a counter-affidavit.
"Such provision prima facie seems to be directly in teeth of law laid down in Prakash Singh.
In the event of the rule being annulled, appointment of Smt.
Tadasha Mishra, DGP of Jharkhand, would be required to be set aside.
We therefore deem it apt.

stories.title: Supreme Court to hear on Oct. 9 Punjab appeal against HC order for CBI probe into corruption allegations
stories.summary: Justice Dipankar Datta said the file has to be studied by puisne judge on the Bench, Justice Sheel Nagu
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court re-scheduled by a day an appeal filed by the State of Punjab against a State High Court order for a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Bhagwant Singh Mann’s office.

Justice Dipankar Datta, heading a Division Bench before which the case came up for hearing on Thursday (October 8, 2026), said the case file was still to “reach” the puisne judge, Justice Sheel Nagu, who was the Chief Justice of Punjab and Haryana High Court before his appointment to the apex court.
Justice Nagu wanted to go through the case file once it reached him.
Senior advocates Vikas Singh and Shadan Farasat, appearing for the State government, sought an interim order to stay the High Court direction.
But Justice Datta pointed out that it was premature to seek an order even before both judges on the Bench had the case file.
The case was listed for October 9.
In an oral mentioning, Mr. Singh had said the High Court order of October 5, for a CBI probe and report within two months, violated the very basic principles of federalism.
He said that sending a Central agency into the poll-bound State, where general consent under Section 6 of the Delhi Special.
Police Establishment (DSPE) Act stood withdrawn since November 8, 2020, was erroneous.

Mr. Singh said the High Court had erroneously directed registration of an FIR into decisions of public servants on transfers, tenders and policy without the previous approval mandated by Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act.

The State of Punjab, in its appeal before the apex court, said the High Court direction for a CBI probe suffered from errors such as treating information shared under Section 66(2) of the PMLA as a direction that makes registration “inevitable”, contrary to the 2022 decision of the apex court in the Vijay Madanlal Choudhary case.
The High Court had directed the CBI to probe corruption allegations linked to Chief Minister Mann’s office.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Mulls Dedicated Corpus For Financial Assistance To Spinal Muscular Atrophy Patients
stories.title: Supreme Court Mulls Dedicated Corpus For Financial Assistance To Spinal Muscular Atrophy Patients
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court today called for suggestions on the creation of a dedicated corpus for providing financial assistance to people suffering from Spinal Muscular Atrophy, a rare genetic disorder.
A bench of CJI Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohana was dealing with a suo motu case taken up over lack of adequate and systematic treatment for SMA patients.
Senior Advocate Aparajita Singh (appointed as Amicus Curiae) and ASG Anil Kaushik appeared.

The case is an offshoot of the proceedings related to comedian Samay Raina and others, who were accused by M/s Cure SMA Foundation of making insensitive jokes about Persons with Disabilities (including those suffering from SMA).
After certain directions by the Court, the comedians apologized and took steps for making amends.
Thereafter, the proceedings were closed and the Court took up the present suo motu case to address the issue of systematic issues in treatment of SMA.
During today's hearing, the CJI asked the Union and the Amicus to suggest a proposal for establishing a dedicated corpus.
The judge expressed that the proposed corpus can include CSR contributions and government grants, but it should be permanent and not incidental in nature.
"it should not depend on the incidental circumstance that today CSR has come or upon persuasion, the government has released the grant...that should not be the case.
But what is the regular channel...a permanent system...kind of an automated nudge to contribution", CJI said.
The judge underlined that the focus should be more towards optimal utilization of the fund, instead of generating the fund.

The bench took suo motu cognisance following reports of a series of sexual offences against minor girls and women in Delhi-NCR, referring to the alleged gangrape of a 17-year-old girl at Aastha Kunj Park, the alleged gangrape and murder of a teenage girl in Swaroop Nagar, and the alleged sexual assault of a minor girl in a moving sleeper bus.
The bus travelled over 47 km from Greater Noida to Delhi without being intercepted.

The bench stated that these incidents pointed to a systematic failure on the part of law enforcement and public administrative authorities to guarantee basic public safety, adding that expressions of solidarity were not enough and that accountability had to be fixed on the authorities.

Senior Advocate Liz Mathew was appointed as amicus.
“The purpose of the present proceedings and the directions issued herein is not to multiply protocols or to create another layer of administrative compliance.

Rather, it is to ascertain whether the mechanisms already devised by the police are operating as living instruments of preventive policing or have those remained substantially confined to the realm of mere paperwork,” it observed on Monday.
Before the bench, Mathew submitted that there was an immediate need for enhanced beat patrolling across Delhi.
She also pointed to the 2020 Comptroller and Auditor General's Report which highlighted a shortage of around 39% in police staff across active duties such as beat patrol and investigation.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court today(October 8) adjourned till tomorrow the plea filed by the Punjab Government challenging the Punjab and Haryana High Court's order directing the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to register a criminal case and probe allegations of corruption linked to the office of Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann.
The matter was listed before a bench comprising Justice Dipankar Datta and Justice Sheel Nagu.
As soon as the matter was taken, Justice Datta said that the matter will be taken tomorrow, as the file reached Justice Nagu late.

When Senior Advocate Vikas Singh, for the State, requested that an interim order be passed against precipitative steps, Justice Datta asked how can it be passed when the other Judge did not get the opportunity to study the files.
The matter was accordingly listed tomorrow.
The State government filed the Special Leave Petition (SLP), challenging the order passed by the High Court on Monday.
On Tuesday, Singh had mentioned the matter before the Chief Justice of India seeking urgent listing.
Singh had then claimed that the case was politically motivated, and was being pursued only since the State is going for elections soon.
Singh had submitted before the CJI that the High Court passed the direction on the ground that the State.
Police did not act on the information furnished by the Enforcement Directorate in terms of Section 66(2) of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act.

He contended that the police need to act only if the information discloses a cognizable offence, and claimed that the High Court direction was contrary to the Supreme Court's judgment in Vijay Madanlal Chaudhary.
The CJI, while turning down the request for same day listing, agreed to list the matter on Thursday.

stories.headline: Odisha bandh: Normal life disrupted in INDIA bloc observes 12-hr strike; BJD stays away | WATCH
stories.title: Odisha bandh: Normal life disrupted in INDIA bloc observes 12-hr strike; BJD stays away | WATCH
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: A 12-hour state-wide bandh called by INDIA bloc parties on Thursday disrupted daily life across several parts of Odisha, with commercial hubs and train services hit, even as the Naveen Patnaik-led BJD distanced itself from the shutdown.
Bhubaneswar: Normal life was affected across parts of Odisha on Thursday as opposition parties under the INDIA bloc banner observed a 12-hour state-wide bandh.

The shutdown was called to demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists, as well as the step-down of Odisha School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over extensive errors in school textbooks and grievances surrounding new mining laws.
In cities like Sambalpur, public transport, educational institutions and commercial establishments remained closed.
Rail operations experienced disruptions after Congress demonstrators halted the Sambalpur-Puri train as part of their protest.

Ahead of the shutdown, opposition leaders led torchlight rallies, with Odisha Pradesh Congress Committee chief Bhakta Charan Das framing the bandh as a struggle to protect constitutional and land rights.
To prevent law and order issues, police deployed nearly 150 officers across the Bhubaneswar-Cuttack region, securing national highways, railway stations and emergency services.
Despite the widespread mobilisation by nine opposition constituents, including the Congress, Left parties, Samajwadi Party and RJD, the Biju Janata Dal (BJD) consciously chose not to participate.

Reaffirming its policy of maintaining equal distance from both the BJP and Congress, BJD leadership clarified that while the party independently opposes the controversial MMDR Amendment Act and textbook errors, it would neither support nor oppose the INDIA bloc’s strike call.

Meanwhile, state administration officials and security personnel remained on high alert across districts to maintain public order and ensure the unhindered movement of healthcare and essential services throughout the strike.
